_note: Consumed by run_jev.py. State uses keyed objects (spec.R1, never spec[0]) to avoid the positional-index pitfall.

spec.R1: Never wake the sender for its own message (compare sender agent ID with the agent's ID).
spec.R2: A closed agent is never woken, whatever else is true about it (closed outranks busy).
spec.R3: Skip if the agent's LastWokenSeq is greater than OR EQUAL to the message seq.
spec.R4: Swarm messages reach everyone. A directed message reaches only the named recipient. A board-wide non-swarm message reaches only the orchestrator.
spec.R5: Agent-sent acknowledgements never wake anyone. Human-sent messages may wake even if they are acks.
spec.R6: A paused project defers agent-sent messages. Human-sent messages still wake.
spec.R7: A retired agent resumes only for a message directed to it by name when ResumeRetiredOnDirect is on; otherwise it is skipped. Swarm broadcasts do not resume retired agents.
spec.R8: A busy active agent is deferred.
spec.R9: At most MaxWakes wakes per agent in the trailing Window; when limited, RetryAt = OLDEST in-window wake time + Window. Human messages bypass the limit.
spec.precedence: Rules apply in order R1..R9; the first matching rule decides.

r2.q: `code` correctly implements `spec.R2`, including when the agent is also busy.

r3.q: `code` correctly implements `spec.R3`, including the equal case.

r4.q: `code` correctly implements `spec.R4` for all three message kinds.

r9.q: `code` correctly implements `spec.R9`, including how RetryAt is computed.

order.q: `code` evaluates the rules in the order required by `spec.precedence`.

violated.q: Which single rule in `spec` does `code` violate?

overall.q: How correct is `code` against the whole `spec`?
